status: Five-rank path audit batch complete. Three defects in the only never-run code path were found and fixed, one of them live-reproduced on this machine and its fix pinned by a new per-device case. (1) rank_write_kernel published ready to the BASE pointer: all five ranks stomped ready[0] and ready[1..4] never arrived, so the five-card case would have waited out the whole 5 s deadline in round 1 and attributed a phantom stall to rank 1 on the operator's machine — the entire trip would have produced a spurious failure. Fixed to &ready[rank]; the /tmp reproduction showed ready=[1,0,0,0,0] on the live device. (2) run_five_rank's setup-failure pre-check tested record.ordinal < 0, which run_probe's catch always writes non-negative before the five-rank case runs: a broken card on the real machine would be launched into, then misreported as a stall. The check now reads the device_identity outcome and the mapped capability bit instead, so a bad card is attributed before the first kernel launch (the bench got the same mapped guard). (3) The zero-device branch returned exit 0 with qualification=fail; it now returns 1 like the enumeration-failure branch (the zero branch is defensive on ROCm 7.2.4, which errors inside hipGetDeviceCount instead of returning zero). New case five_rank_indexing (registry 24 -> 25, appended) runs the exact cross-device kernel and guarded layout with five streams on ONE device, verifying every rank's payload word and its own ready word for the whole round count; the five-device case and this case now share one rounds protocol (run_rank_rounds), so the loop that will run on the real machine is the same code pinned on every dev machine. Falsification on a scratch worktree with the bug re-injected: five_rank_indexing=fail, 'rank 1 did not publish ready in round 1 within 5 s', exit 1, run bounded — the regression net provably discriminates. HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES semantics measured: canonical form 0,1,2,3,4 and a trailing comma work; leading/trailing whitespace or an empty value make enumeration error (report still written, exit 1) — documented in the operator README section so a typo can no longer masquerade as a broken machine.
